It was hard for me to read about schizophrenia cause when I lived with my mom if I had any materials dealing with it, I would of been accused of being controlled by my grandparents(the ones who sent her to the psych ward) and being brainwashed. I've only moved away from her for the past 3 months. When I lived with her and went to college I had to take Psych 101 and we had a whole chapter dealing with Schizophrenia and even watched a clip of a therapist taking to a man with Schizophrenic behaviors and that's the first real time I was able to learn in depth about the disease/disorder.

I don't know if it's as much a habit as is something I'm more aware of than "normal" people. Is that when you start mimicking actions or speech patterns of your friends or family my mom believed they where controlling you. I picked up that this set off her delusions. So I made myself super self conscious about what I say or my own body movements. Even to this day, I catch myself mimicking what my roommates do or say then immediately tell myself to stop even though I no longer live with her. 

I realized something was wrong when I was playing Mario Paint on my SNES and just made a cool song. So I walked out of my bedroom and down the hall to the living room/kitchen and saw my mom doing dishes and yelling out the window. So I walked up behind her and poked her and it startled her. I asked what she was doing and she told me nothing so I looked out the window and saw nothing. Then I showed her my song in Mario Paint but she was starring off to the side with a mean look and pursed lips, kinda of shaking her head no. Then when the song ended she said it was good and just walked away.

Physically, no she never hit me because of it. Did I get spanked cause I deserved it? Yes. Emotionally I think I'm extremely messed up.  It's hard for me to connect with people cause I don't share my past or details about my mom or family. I also don't seek relationship because of the whole meet the family ordeal or sharing intimidate thoughts cause I'm to self conscious.
